name: MIDORI.so Shibuya
card: Four floors of workspace and a library in Sakuragaoka, 4 minutes from Shibuya Station
title: MIDORI.so Shibuya — coworking with a lounge and library on floors 3–6 in Sakuragaokacho, Shibuya
lead: MIDORI.so Shibuya is in Sakuragaokacho, a four-minute walk from Shibuya Station. Across four floors, from the 3rd to the 6th, there are workspaces, a lounge, a kitchen, a library, meeting rooms, private booths and private rooms. It is run by MIRAI INSTITUTE, which also operates the Nakameguro and Nagatacho sites. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 3F workspace, lounge, kitchen / 4F workspace, meeting rooms, booths / 5F workspace, booths, lounge / 6F private rooms
concept: Four floors to choose from, in Shibuya's Sakuragaoka

MIDORI.so is a coworking community exploring “the future of work in a society that values the individual”. The Shibuya site is in a corner of Sakuragaoka, an area being redeveloped, with workspaces and lounges over four floors.

The 3rd floor has the lounge and kitchen where people gather, the 4th and 5th have workspaces and booths for focus, and the 6th has private rooms. The higher you go, the quieter it gets — so you can choose where to be according to the day's work.
steps: The library lets you work surrounded by bookshelves.
A free desk is ¥44,000 a month, a fixed desk ¥60,500 a month and a private booth from ¥71,500 a month (all with an ¥11,000 sign-up fee), available 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
The 4th floor has a workspace, meeting rooms and private booths; the 5th has a workspace, private booths and a lounge.
Pop-in is ¥3,300 a day or ¥33,000 for an 11-day pack, usable 10:00–18:00.

word.title: What is a private booth?
body: A semi-private seat inside the coworking space, for one person or a small team. At MIDORI.so Shibuya they are on the 4th and 5th floors.
It sits between a free desk and a private room: you keep your own spot while still feeling the atmosphere of the shared space.

name: MIDORI.so Aoyama
card: No fixed desks — a space built around meeting people
title: MIDORI.so Aoyama — a workspace and bar without fixed seats, built for meeting people, on the 2nd and 3rd floors in Minami-Aoyama 1-chome
lead: MIDORI.so Aoyama is in Minami-Aoyama 1-chome, a four-minute walk from Aoyama-itchome Station. With no fixed desks, it is a workspace that rethinks work by focusing on meeting people. The 2nd floor has a listening lounge and a bar, the roof has a garden overlooking Aoba Park, and the ground floor houses Ohizumi Factory's BROOKS. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 1F BROOKS (café & restaurant) / 2F workspace, listening lounge, bar / 3F members' area / rooftop garden
concept: Rethinking work through meeting people
MIDORI.so Aoyama is a workspace without fixed desks. The website describes it as a place to rethink “working” by focusing on “meeting”.

From 9:00 to 18:00 it is a salon; from 18:00 to 22:00, a bar. The same room turns from a place of work into a place for conversation as the day goes on. The sound system in the 2nd-floor listening lounge is by KOMATSU ONKYO.
steps: A floor with no fixed seats
The 2nd floor is a workspace without fixed seats; choose where to sit according to your plans for the day.
A free desk is ¥44,000 a month (sign-up fee ¥11,000).
A room built for sound, and a bar at night
The 2nd-floor listening lounge is for listening to music on a KOMATSU ONKYO sound system.
From 18:00 it becomes a bar. The lounge can be hired: 89.0 m², up to 30 seated or 45 standing.

word.title: What is a listening lounge?
body: A room acoustically tuned for listening to music well. At MIDORI.so Aoyama it is on the 2nd floor, with sound by KOMATSU ONKYO.
Putting a room for music in a workplace values something other than efficiency. Here, the reason to gather is created by sound, not desks.

name: MIDORI.so Kichijoji
card: Coworking on the 8th floor of Kichijoji PARCO
title: MIDORI.so Kichijoji — coworking on the 8th floor of Kichijoji PARCO, where a small community meets the open air of a department store
lead: MIDORI.so Kichijoji is on the 8th floor of Kichijoji PARCO, a two-minute walk from Kichijoji Station. It is MIDORI.so's first site outside Tokyo's 23 wards. Workspace, meeting rooms, a kitchen, a lounge and booths are all on one floor, open every day from 8:00 to 23:00. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Workspace / meeting rooms / kitchen / lounge / booths
concept: A close-knit community and the open air of a shopping building

The website describes MIDORI.so Kichijoji as “a place where a community where everyone knows each other mixes with the open atmosphere of a commercial building”. It is on the 8th floor of Kichijoji PARCO, a building shoppers pass through too.
It is MIDORI.so's first site outside the 23 wards — a place for people who would rather work by the station in their own neighbourhood than commute into central Tokyo.
steps: The workspace has shared desks and fixed desks.
A free desk is ¥33,000 a month, a fixed desk ¥47,300 a month and a private booth from ¥66,000 a month (all with an ¥11,000 sign-up fee).
A place to eat and a place to talk
The kitchen is a shared space for members.
Meeting rooms are available for discussions, so work and conversation happen on the same floor.
Evening-and-weekend membership, and pop-in from two hours
An evening-and-weekend free desk, usable weekdays 17:00–23:00 and on weekends and holidays, is ¥22,000 a month.
Pop-in is ¥1,100 for two hours, ¥2,200 a day or ¥22,000 for an 11-day pack, usable 10:00–18:00. Kichijoji Station is a two-minute walk.

word.title: What is evening-and-weekend membership?
body: A plan you can use only on weekday evenings and on weekends and holidays. At MIDORI.so Kichijoji it costs ¥22,000 a month.
It is for people who keep a day job and work on their own projects at night and at weekends — a plan that makes sense precisely because the space is by the station where they live.

name: MIDORI.so Nihonbashi
card: Work and sleep under the same roof
title: MIDORI.so Nihonbashi — a café and bar on the ground floor and a dormitory where you can stay while you work, in Higashi-Nihonbashi 3-chome
lead: MIDORI.so Nihonbashi is in Higashi-Nihonbashi 3-chome, a one-minute walk from Bakuro-yokoyama and Higashi-Nihonbashi stations. With a café, bar and gallery on the ground floor, a lounge on the 2nd and semi-private dormitory rooms for working and sleeping on the 3rd and 4th, it is a place where working and staying live together. There is no sign-up fee or membership: you use it through day and night pop-in. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 1F café, bar, gallery, reception / 2F lounge, mini kitchen / 3F–4F rooms for working and sleeping
Day pop-in ¥2,200 / Night pop-in ¥8,800 per night (no sign-up fee or membership)
concept: Work and rest, without hurrying

MIDORI.so Nihonbashi combines a lounge, dormitory-like rooms and a ground-floor café and bar. Working and staying share one building, which the website says supports a way of “working and resting gently, without hurrying”.
It is not membership-based: you use it through day pop-in (10:00–18:00) and night pop-in (18:00 to 9:30 the next morning). You can carry on working and simply stay the night.
steps: An entrance open to the street
The ground floor has a café, bar, gallery and reception. Guests, workers and neighbours all pass through here first.
Bakuro-yokoyama and Higashi-Nihonbashi stations are both a one-minute walk away.
The 3rd and 4th floors are semi-private rooms for working and sleeping. Night pop-in costs ¥8,800 per night.
Rooms for working and sleeping on the same floor are rare even among coworking spaces.

word.title: What is a dormitory?
body: A shared, hostel-style way of staying, where several people sleep in the same room or on the same floor. At MIDORI.so Nihonbashi, the 3rd and 4th floors are semi-private dormitories for working and sleeping.
Adding a place to sleep to a place to work changes things for people who come from far away — or who are up against a deadline.

name: Business-Airport Kudanshita
card: On the ground floor of Kudan Kaikan Terrace, facing the greenery and water of the Imperial moat
title: Business-Airport Kudanshita — a workplace carrying on history, on the ground floor of Kudan Kaikan Terrace overlooking the moat
lead: Business-Airport Kudanshita, run by Tokyu Land, is on the ground floor of Kudan Kaikan Terrace, in front of Kudanshita Station. Overlooking the lush greenery and water of the Imperial Palace moat, it is a workplace that inherits and makes use of history while answering new ways of working. Coworking is open 7:00–22:00 on weekdays, and the serviced offices 24 hours. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Serviced office ROOM (1–15 people) and DESK / coworking / meeting room
Coworking weekdays 7:00–22:00 (closed weekends and holidays) / serviced offices 24 hours
concept: Innovation and creativity, in the heart of Tokyo

The website's slogan is “Innovation and creativity in the heart of Tokyo”. In front of Kudanshita Station, facing the moat, it looks out over rich greenery and water — a workplace that carries history forward while meeting the new needs of the times.
Business-Airport is Tokyu Land's shared-office brand, named after an airport where diverse people gather and depart. Kudanshita is the site set on the ground floor of a historic building.
steps: Coworking is available 7:00–22:00 on weekdays (reception 9:00–18:00). It is closed on weekends and holidays.
Address membership is ¥82,500 a month, Master membership ¥38,500 and Private membership ¥14,300.
Serviced-office ROOMs for 1–15 people start at ¥176,000 a month; DESKs for 1–2 start at ¥104,500.
Serviced offices can be entered 24 hours a day.
Meeting room A seats 8 and costs ¥3,300 an hour.
Hold your meetings with a view of the moat's greenery and water.

word.title: What is a serviced office?
body: A private office with furniture, equipment and reception staff already in place, rented by the month. Business-Airport calls them ROOM and DESK.
The advantage is having shared coworking and a closed private room in the same building. As the team grows, it can keep working in the same place.

name: Business-Airport Daikanyama
card: A green workplace on the 3rd floor of Forestgate Daikanyama
title: Business-Airport Daikanyama — a base among the trees where buzz and calm coexist, on the 3rd floor of Forestgate Daikanyama MAIN
lead: Business-Airport Daikanyama, run by Tokyu Land, is on the 3rd floor of the MAIN building of Forestgate Daikanyama in Daikanyamacho. The website describes a place where buzz and calm coexist seamlessly and where encounters between all kinds of people take root. Surrounded by greenery, it supports original ideas and the first shoots of new businesses. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Coworking weekdays 7:00–22:00, Saturdays 10:00–18:00 (closed Sundays and holidays) / serviced offices 24 hours
concept: Where buzz and calm coexist seamlessly

The website describes Business-Airport Daikanyama as a place where “liveliness and calm coexist seamlessly, and encounters with all kinds of people take root”. A space surrounded by greenery, it says, inspires distinctive ideas and supports new businesses as they sprout.
Forestgate Daikanyama is a mixed-use complex in Daikanyamacho. On the 3rd floor of its MAIN building are private rooms, booths, fixed desks and coworking.
steps: From 7:00 on weekdays, and open on Saturdays
Coworking is open 7:00–22:00 on weekdays (reception 9:00–18:00) and 10:00–18:00 on Saturdays.
Address membership is ¥82,500 a month, Master ¥38,500, Private ¥14,300, and Flex membership ¥550 per 30 minutes.
Private ROOMs start at ¥165,000 a month, BOOTHs at ¥220,000 and fixed DESKs at ¥110,000.
Serviced offices can be entered 24 hours a day.
Being surrounded by greenery is what defines this site.
The calm of Daikanyama's streets and the buzz of the building mix on the same floor.

word.title: What is Flex membership?
body: A membership where you pay only for the time you use. At Business-Airport Daikanyama it costs ¥550 per 30 minutes.
It is a way to find out how often you will use the space before committing to a monthly plan.

name: Business-Airport Shibuya Sakura Stage
card: A calm space in an exciting city, on the 7th floor of Shibuya Sakura Stage
title: Business-Airport Shibuya Sakura Stage — a Shibuya workplace where people, culture and the world cross paths, on the 7th floor of SHIBUYA Tower
lead: Business-Airport Shibuya Sakura Stage, run by Tokyu Land, is on the 7th floor of SHIBUYA Tower at Shibuya Sakura Stage, close to Shibuya Station. Under the slogan “the future gathers in cutting-edge Shibuya, overflowing with creative sensibility”, it aims to be a space where body and mind feel at ease in the middle of an exciting city. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: ROOM (private) / DESK (fixed seat) / Workers' Lounge / meeting rooms / event space
Workers' Lounge weekdays 7:00–22:00, weekends and holidays 10:00–18:00 / serviced offices 24 hours
concept: In Shibuya, where people, culture, value and the world intersect

The website writes that “the future gathers in cutting-edge Shibuya, overflowing with creative sensibility”. In Shibuya, where people, culture, value and the world intersect, it aims to offer a rare space where body and mind can feel at ease.

The shared area is called the “SHIBUYA Well Center Workers' Lounge” and is open on weekends and holidays as well as weekdays. Private rooms, fixed desks, meeting rooms and an event space are all on the same floor.
steps: A shared space open on weekends too
The Workers' Lounge is open 7:00–22:00 on weekdays (reception 9:00–18:00) and 10:00–18:00 on weekends and holidays.
Address membership is ¥99,000 a month, Master ¥38,500, Private ¥14,300, and Flex ¥550 per 30 minutes.
Private ROOMs start at ¥198,000 a month and fixed DESKs at ¥143,000.
Serviced offices can be entered 24 hours a day.
A room for six, and a place for events
Meeting room A for six costs ¥2,750 an hour, and the one-person online meeting room ¥550 per 30 minutes.
The event space costs ¥33,000 an hour for members and ¥49,500 an hour for non-members.

word.title: What is the Workers' Lounge?
body: The name of the shared workspace at Business-Airport Shibuya Sakura Stage, officially the “SHIBUYA Well Center Workers' Lounge”.
Putting the word “well” in the name shows the intention: a place to rest body and mind in stimulating Shibuya.
